title: Myth, Legend, Fable and Folk Tale
objective: After this level you can tell a myth from a legend, a fable (like Aesop's) and a folk tale.
summary: A fable is an animal tale with a moral, like Aesop's fox and the "sour grapes". A myth is a sacred traditional story, a legend is told as history, and folk tales change with each teller.

cards.headline: Say "sour grapes" and you're quoting a fox.
cards.body: In an old fable, a fox jumps again and again for a bunch of grapes and misses every time. Finally he walks off, calling them sour grapes, not worth the trouble. That's a fable. It's one of four kinds of traditional story people mix up all the time. Here's how to tell them apart.

cards.fact: A fable teaches a lesson, and usually tells you what it is.
cards.context: Fables usually star animals that talk and act like people, and they poke at human follies. A moral is woven in, often stated at the end. The fox's, in The Aesop for Children (1919): "There are many who pretend to despise and belittle that which is beyond their reach." Most famous fables are credited to Aesop, a likely legendary Greek; the earliest known collection under his name dates to the 4th century BCE.

items.label: Myth

Told as a matter of history

items.label: Folk tale

Changes as tellers pass it on

cards.headline: Told as history, true or not
cards.body: The key to a legend is that it's told as history. William Tell, Switzerland's hero of freedom, is said to have shot an apple off his son's head. The story is tied to a real country and a real struggle, yet there's no evidence Tell ever existed. And a myth isn't a polite word for a lie. Scholars use it for a traditional sacred story. In this tree, myth never means false.

cards.headline: Four kinds of story: sorted
learned: Fable: animals, follies and a moral
Myth: a traditional story tied to religious belief
Legend: told as history, true or not
Folk tale: changes with every teller

questions.prompt: What does a fable weave into its story, often stating it at the end?

options.label: A moral, a lesson about behavior
The family tree of the gods
options.rationale: That sounds more like a myth.

options.label: A map of the hero's homeland
options.rationale: Fables are short and not about places.

questions.explanation: A fable usually stars animals acting like people and carries a moral, often stated at the end.

questions.prompt: There is no evidence William Tell existed. Why is his story still called a legend?

options.label: It stars talking animals and ends with a moral
It is a sacred story about the gods
It is a fairy tale meant for small children
It is told as history, about a particular person and place

questions.explanation: A legend is a traditional story about a particular person or place, told as a matter of history, whether or not it happened.

questions.prompt: Level 1 said oral literature is passed on by voice. Which kind of story is known for changing as tellers pass it on?

options.label: A fable with its stated moral
options.rationale: Fables are known for their morals.

options.label: A legend told as history
options.rationale: Legends are known for being told as history.

options.label: A novel
options.rationale: A novel is a written, invented prose story.

questions.explanation: Folk tales are found almost everywhere and keep changing as tellers pass them on: oral literature in action.
